## Objective
- Build a complete playable game inspired by a unique Brazilian Far West setting.
- The user now wants the campaign to mirror *Red Dead Redemption 2*’s campaign.

## Requirements
- Initial request: “A unique Brasilian far West game like red dead”.
- Build request specified: build a complete playable game without clarifying questions.
- Follow-up: “Make real life graphics and physics”.
- Latest request: “Mirror red dead redemption 2 campaign”.

## Decisions
- Created an original Brazilian sertão frontier story and game titled *Sertão — The Last Train* rather than copying *Red Dead Redemption 2* directly.
- Added momentum-based movement, collisions, and painterly lighting to the canvas game.
- Began adapting the game toward a multi-chapter campaign, retaining the original setting and characters.

## Work State
### Completed
- Created initial game UI and canvas game in `index.html`, `style.css`, and `game.js`.
- Added movement, aiming, shooting, enemies, clues, station objective, win/lose screens, pause/reload controls, and custom-drawn sertão scenery.
- Added inertia, drag, solid cover collisions, enemy movement physics, enemy separation, shadows, and warm atmospheric overlays.
- Added an initial campaign transition modal element to `index.html`.

### Active
- Implement campaign progression corresponding to the latest request, using original characters, missions, locations, and plot rather than duplicating RDR2’s story.
- The campaign modal in `index.html` currently has a Continue button, but no associated campaign logic exists yet.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Inspect current `game.js` and `index.html` campaign/modal state.
2. Implement campaign chapters and progression, updating story, mission objectives, encounters, and transitions while keeping the Brazilian frontier setting original.
3. Test syntax and play flow; verify chapter progression and restart/continue controls.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game UI, overlays, campaign screen markup.
- `game.js`: Game logic, physics, rendering, mission and campaign progression.
- `style.css`: Game presentation and overlays.

## Important Context
- Latest edit added `#campaign-screen`, `#campaign-kicker`, `#campaign-title`, `#campaign-copy`, and `#continue-button` in `index.html`; campaign functionality is not implemented.
- Previous `node --check game.js` passed before the latest campaign markup edit.
- Changes are uncommitted.

## Objective
- Build a complete playable Brazilian frontier game with an original multi-chapter campaign.
- Make Minas Gerais the setting, with Ouro Preto as the game’s largest city.

## Requirements
- “A unique Brasilian far West game like red dead”.
- “build a complete playable game without clarifying questions.”
- “Make real life graphics and physics”.
- “Mirror red dead redemption 2 campaign” while preserving an original story, characters, and setting.
- “Make the city of ouro preto as the biggest city of the game”.
- “Make the game in minas gerais”.

## Decisions
- The game is titled *Sertão — The Last Train* and uses an original Brazilian frontier story instead of copying RDR2’s plot.
- A five-chapter campaign is being added, with chapter-specific objectives and an original finale in Ouro Preto.

## Work State
### Completed
- Created a canvas game with movement, aiming, shooting, enemies, clues, collision, HUD, pause/reload, and start/end screens.
- Added momentum-based movement, collisions, enemy movement/separation, and atmospheric rendering.
- Added five original campaign chapter definitions and partial chapter transition/objective logic.
- Updated several visible labels from Bahia to Minas Gerais and changed the final campaign text to reference Ouro Preto.
- Added a dense grid of Ouro Preto city buildings and streets to the eastern part of the map.

### Active
- Finish and verify campaign progression and objective behavior.
- Complete the Minas Gerais setting and make Ouro Preto visibly and functionally the largest city; the current map still uses sertão/caatinga visuals and some Bahia-era naming.
- Verify city building rendering/collision and ensure the city destination is reachable.

### Blocked
- (none)

1. Inspect current `game.js` for incomplete campaign changes and syntax/runtime issues.
2. Finish chapter objective tracking, transitions, HUD updates, and final/restart behavior; run syntax and gameplay checks.
3. Improve and verify Ouro Preto’s city visuals, landmarks, street layout, and collision; update remaining setting text and locations to Minas Gerais.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: Game world, campaign chapters, objectives, rendering, city layout, and gameplay logic.
- `index.html`: HUD, chapter labels, campaign screens, and Minas Gerais branding.
- `style.css`: Game presentation and overlays.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; no checks were run after the latest edits.
- The city grid is currently placed around x=1600–2390 on a 2400-wide map; city buildings are also added to `cover`, making them collision obstacles.
- Chapter I still begins in the caatinga; the map’s existing background and some locations retain sertão/desert styling.

## Objective
- Build a complete playable Brazilian frontier campaign set in Minas Gerais, with Ouro Preto as its largest city.
- Convert the existing game to 3D.

## Requirements
- Original Brazilian frontier game with a multi-chapter campaign and playable gameplay.
- Minas Gerais setting; Ouro Preto should be the largest city.
- Realistic-looking graphics and physics.
- The story should be inspired by the requested campaign scope but use original characters, story, and setting.
- Make the game in 3D.

## Decisions
- The game is titled *Sertão — The Last Train* and uses an original story rather than copying *Red Dead Redemption 2*.
- A five-chapter campaign uses original objectives and ends in Ouro Preto.
- The 3D conversion is being implemented with Three.js from a jsDelivr ES module URL.

## Work State
### Completed
- Existing 2D game includes movement, shooting, enemies, clues, HUD, pause/reload, and start/end screens.
- Five chapter definitions and partial objective/transition logic are present.
- Minas Gerais branding, an Ouro Preto destination, and a dense city layout were added.
- Initial Three.js setup, lighting, camera, 3D city/building and character construction, and ground-plane aiming code were added to `game.js`.

### Active
- Finish the 3D conversion: replace the old canvas 2D drawing/render loop with Three.js scene rendering and update effects, actors, markers, and camera behavior.
- Resolve leftover references to the removed 2D `ctx` and old 2D camera state; the current code is likely to error at runtime.
- Verify shooting, collisions, city reachability, campaign progression, and restart behavior after conversion.
- Improve Minas Gerais/Ouro Preto surroundings, since existing setting still includes caatinga/sertão descriptions and desert-like scenery.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Inspect the latest `game.js` and complete the Three.js render loop, replacing remaining 2D canvas drawing calls and camera-dependent logic.
2. Run syntax/runtime checks and fix errors; verify pointer aiming and firing against 3D enemies.
3. Test campaign objectives and transitions, then verify Ouro Preto’s buildings, collision, and reachable destination in-browser.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: Campaign, gameplay state, Three.js initialization and in-progress 3D conversion.
- `index.html`: Game HUD, campaign screens, and Minas Gerais branding.
- `style.css`: Game presentation and overlays.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; no checks were run after the latest 3D edits.
- `game.js` now imports Three.js from `https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.180.0/build/three.module.js`, but still contains old canvas 2D rendering code.
- The previous 2D view used `camera.x`/`camera.y`; the new 3D code introduces `camera3d`, raycasting, and Three.js actor meshes.
